newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar emir to visit U.S. on Mideast summit.
newsitem.headline: Qatar emir to visit U.S. on Mideast summit.

text.p: Qatar's emir will visit Washington in the second week of June to discuss preparations for a Middle East-North Africa (MENA) economic summit set for November in Doha, officials said on Wednesday.

Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa al-Thani would meet President Bill Clinton and other top administration officials during the official visit, his first to the United States since he toppled his father in a bloodless palace coup in 1995.
"It is an official visit. The emir will meet with President Clinton to discuss the forthcoming economic summit," one official said.
The United States, the main sponsor of the peace process, said earlier this month it was working closely with Qatar to prepare for the economic forum.
Sheikh Hamad is expected to leave for Washington around June 10, the officials said. Both countries enjoy strong economic and military links.

Syria and some Gulf Arab states favour postponing the MENA summit, attended by Israel, Arab and Western countries, until the resumption of the stalled Middle East peace talks, diplomats and official Gulf sources have said.
Arabs have been angered by Israel's building of a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

Qatar said it was going ahead with preparations for the summit but has suggested that Israel's invitation depended on the resumption Arab-Israeli talks under a six-year-old process co-sponsored by Washington and Moscow.
Israel attended previous MENA summits held in Casablanca, Amman and Cairo.
